title: Elementary submodels: Tarski–Vaught and Löwenheim–Skolem
summary: Find smaller structures that agree on every first-order formula with parameters, using the witness criterion and downward Löwenheim–Skolem.
abstract: Can an uncountable structure contain a countable part that gives the same answers to every first-order question about its elements? In a countable language, it can. Simply restricting the domain is not enough: removing zero from the natural-number order leaves one with no smaller element. An elementary submodel avoids such changes in truth. The Tarski–Vaught criterion reduces the task to retaining a witness for every existential statement true in the larger structure with parameters already present. Repeatedly adding chosen witnesses yields the downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem, including a size bound for larger languages and a way to retain any prescribed set of elements.
